claims.claim: The BC Conservatives were leading in 64 of 93 districts, the NDP in 27 and the Greens in two.
claims.episode_span: leading in 64 of 93 districts to the NDP’s 27 and the Greens’ two
claims.source_title: David Eby steps down as BC NDP leader after snap election defeat
claims.supporting_quote: By late election night, the Conservatives were leading in 64 of British Columbia’s 93 electoral districts, compared with 27 for the NDP and two for the Greens.

claims.claim: Preliminary results gave the Conservatives 48.05 percent, the NDP 37.38 percent, the Greens 10.97 percent, and turnout was 48.06 percent.
claims.episode_span: Conservative share at 48.05 per cent, the NDP at 37.38 per cent and the Greens at 10.97 per cent, with preliminary turnout at 48.06 per cent
claims.source_title: BC Conservatives win majority government, Eby resigns
claims.supporting_quote: Conservative Party of BC (93 candidates / 48.05% of vote) Leader Lorne Doerkson elected / premier-elect (64 MLAs elected)

claims.claim: David Eby said it was time for new leadership within the BC NDP.
claims.episode_span: it is time for new leadership within our party
claims.source_title: David Eby steps down as BC NDP leader after snap election defeat
claims.supporting_quote: “This is obviously something I do with a very heavy heart. But it is time for new leadership within our party,” he said.

claims.claim: This election recorded 1,770,371 votes, or 47.97 percent of registered voters, compared with 58.74 percent in 2024.
claims.episode_span: 1,770,371 votes, 47.97 per cent of registered voters, against more than two million and 58.74 per cent in 2024
claims.source_title: B.C. Election: 8 take-aways after a landslide Conservative win
claims.supporting_quote: In this election, the vote total amounted to 1,770,371 or 47.97 per cent of registered voters.

claims.claim: Emily Lowan, 26, won Saanich North and the Islands and said the Greens are the only party equipped to stand against the Conservatives and their existence.
claims.episode_span: Green leader Emily Lowan, 26, won Saanich North and the Islands
claims.source_title: Read her full speech: BC Greens leader Emily Lowan attacks incoming Conservative majority government
claims.supporting_quote: “We are the only party who is equipped to stand against the Conservatives and their existence,” she said during her election night speech after the results poured in.

claims.claim: The NDP won eight of 12 Vancouver ridings and lost Vancouver-Langara, Vancouver-Fraserview and Vancouver-Yaletown.
claims.episode_span: The NDP won eight of 12 Vancouver ridings and lost three it held in 2024
claims.source_title: B.C. Election Results: NDP loses ground in Vancouver, but still holds most of city
claims.supporting_quote: On a rough night for the B.C. NDP, the party won eight of 12 ridings in Vancouver.

claims.claim: Niki Sharma beat Phyllis Tang 9,706 votes to 4,794, and Terry Yung lost to Margareta Dovgal by 844 votes.
claims.episode_span: Niki Sharma beat Phyllis Tang 9,706 to 4,794
claims.source_title: B.C. Election Results: NDP loses ground in Vancouver, but still holds most of city
claims.supporting_quote: With all polls reporting, the B.C. NDP’s Niki Sharma beat the Conservatives’ Phyllis Tang with 9,706 votes to 4,794 votes.

claims.episode_span: puck drop at 7:00 p.m. PDT on Sportsnet in Vancouver

claims.claim: Lorne Doerkson had 76.9 percent in Cariboo-Chilcotin with 75 of 89 boxes counted.
claims.episode_span: 76.9 per cent of the vote as of 10:30 p.m. and 75 of 89 ballot boxes counted
claims.source_title: Cariboo-Chilcotin MLA Lorne Doerkson wins re-election for third time in a row, becomes premier-elect
claims.supporting_quote: Based on preliminary polls Doerkson, the incumbent MLA for the Conservative Party of B.C., has won 76.9 per cent of the vote as of 10:30 p.m., with 75 of 89 ballot boxes counted.

claims.claim: Zeeshan Wahla won Surrey-City Centre with 5,696 votes to Amna Shah’s 5,305.
claims.episode_span: Zeeshan Wahla had 5,696 votes, 47.5 per cent, to incumbent Amna Shah’s 5,305
claims.source_title: B.C. VOTES: Wahla wins Surrey-City Centre for Conservatives in rematch with NDP’s Shah
claims.supporting_quote: At 10:46 p.m. Saturday, with all 72 ballot boxes counted, Wahla led with 5,696 votes (47.5%) to Shah’s 5,305 (44.2%).
